title: Why It's Called Owen Field: History of Oklahoma Memorial Stadium
question: Why is Oklahoma's football field called Owen Field?
answer: The playing surface is named for Bennie Owen, OU's coach from 1905 to 1926, who helped raise money for the stadium. The stadium's Memorial name honors university people who died in World War I.
summary: Owen Field honors coach Bennie Owen, and Oklahoma Memorial Stadium honors World War I dead. A short history of the Sooners' home from 1923 to its record crowd.
body: The Sooners' home has two names that mean two different things. Owen Field is the playing surface, named for Bennie Owen, who coached Oklahoma from 1905 to 1926 and helped raise the money to build a real stadium. The full building is Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium, and the Memorial part honors university students and personnel who died in World War I.

It started small. The first game at the site was played on Oct. 20, 1923, a 62-7 Oklahoma win over Washington University, and the only permanent seating was a 500-seat bleacher on the east side. In 1925 a 16,000-seat grandstand went up on the west side, and an east grandstand followed in 1929.
Owen earned the honor. He had unbeaten teams in 1911, 1915 and 1918, and he became a charter member of the College Football Hall of Fame in 1951. After coaching he served as OU's athletic director.

The stadium kept growing alongside the program, with expansions in 1949, 1957, 1975, 2003 and 2016 that added a west upper deck, an east upper deck with suites, and an enclosed south end zone. Artificial turf arrived in 1970, and natural grass came back in 1994. In the early 2000s a $12 million gift from the Gaylord family for renovations added the family name to the stadium.
The biggest crowd in stadium history came on Nov. 11, 2017, when 88,308 fans watched Oklahoma beat TCU 38-20.
